output.answer_markdown: Chesapeake uses oil, natural gas and NGL derivatives to mitigate a portion of its exposure to adverse price changes [1]. It determines the fair value of its derivatives using established index prices, volatility curves and discount factors, and compares these estimates to counterparty valuations for reasonableness [2]. Counterparty non-performance risk is considered in the valuation of its derivatives but has not had a material impact on their values to date [3]. To limit credit risk, it enters derivative contracts only with highly rated counterparties or those it deems to have acceptable credit strength, and attempts to limit exposure to non-performance by any single counterparty [4]. As of December 31, 2020, its derivative instruments were spread among 7 counterparties [5]. Collateral requirements above defined thresholds partially mitigate future counterparty risk [6]. As of December 31, 2020, none of its open derivative instruments were designated as cash flow hedges [7].
